items.title: Around a dozen banking apps began specifically permitting GrapheneOS
items.raw_content: @maya@gs.lexinova.eu @OmegaPolice@hachyderm.io @britter@chaos.social Most banking apps work on GrapheneOS but many have memory corruption bugs and incorrect anti-tampering code requiring our per-app exploit protection compatibility mode toggle. Around 10% of banking apps are unavailable due to banning using a non-Google-approved OS. Around a dozen banking apps began specifically permitting GrapheneOS in addition to a Google-approved OS which is growing. There's a good list based on ongoing user reports: https://privsec.dev/posts/android/banking-applications-compatibility-with-grapheneos/
items.title_zh: 十余家银行应用开始明确允许 GrapheneOS
items.summary: GrapheneOS says most banking apps work on its Android fork, about 10% are unavailable because they ban non-Google-approved operating systems, and around a dozen banks have begun specifically permitting GrapheneOS.

items.title: Why is AI generated language so hard to understand?
items.raw_content: There is a widespread sense that AI-generated text has recently become harder to understand. In this study, we investigate a set of psycholinguistic features that are known to correlate with human processing difficulty (e.g., object relative clauses, long syntactic dependencies, low-frequency n-grams). Using a novel corpus of AI-generated text across diverse domains, we find that AI models use these difficult features more often than paraphrases generated by round-trip translation. Compared with human writing, all nine frontier and near-frontier models use more inanimate subjects with animate
items.title_zh: 为什么 AI 生成的语言这么难懂？
items.summary: A study finds AI-generated text uses features linked to processing difficulty more often than round-trip translation paraphrases, and all nine frontier models tested used more inanimate subjects than human writers.
